modules.name: Station
modules.oneLine: The home device where pods are studied, mibis are grown and families begin.

items.title: Bring pods home and read them
items.text: Dock the Companion, open the bay, identify each pod and read its genome chapter by chapter, then compare two pods of the same species side by side.

items.title: Create and grow a mibi
items.text: Shape the traits you have read, grow the mibi in its bud and open it to meet the juvenile.

items.title: Habitat and the bays
items.text: Six bays hold your mibis, you choose which one comes along with you, and any pod or mibi can be returned to the wild.

items.title: Cross two mibis
items.text: Pick two adults of one species and see what their child could inherit, drawn only from the chapters you have read.

items.title: A new face for every Station screen
items.text: The Station's screens are moving one at a time to the graphics engine the real device will run, starting with Pods and the Library.

items.title: The Library and the field guide
items.text: A tome with a plate for every species you have found and a book per species that fills in as you read more pods.

items.title: Portrait sittings
items.text: Research milestones earn a mibi a sitting for its own portrait, which comes home as a crate at the dock.

items.title: Home, Rest and Idle on the new face
items.text: Home with your residents and its bench, the Rest key, docking and arrivals, and the Idle view that keeps the habitat on show all day.

items.title: The Cross on the new face
items.text: Pick two mibis and see what their child could inherit, chapter by chapter, redrawn on the new face.

items.title: Create and the Incubator on the new face
items.text: Shape a mibi's traits, then watch it grow under the dome leaf by leaf until it is ready to open.

items.title: Habitat and the Probe bench on the new face
items.text: Your resident up close with its card and bays, and the bench where the Probe's Shield is mended and upgraded.

items.title: The family tree
items.text: Each mibi's book will show its lineage once there are enough bred families to design it around.

modules.name: Companion
modules.oneLine: The handheld for exploring a fogged world with your partner and carrying discoveries home.

items.title: Expeditions on a fogged world map
items.text: Every step lifts the fog, and each world turn changes what is out there waiting to be found.

items.title: Survey places with Call
items.text: Places start under a veil that lifts as you walk, and Call sweeps further to reveal pods, stones and creatures.

items.title: Storms, Energy and the Shield
items.text: Storms charge stones with Energy but can strike you in the open, so your Shield and shelter matter.

items.title: Outposts and beacons
items.text: Light an outpost to head home and shelter there, or light a beacon to reveal the land around it.

items.title: Head home with your crates
items.text: Heading home seals what you found into crates in the bay, ready to open at the Station.

items.title: Your partner on the road
items.text: One mibi comes along with you, has its own screen between expeditions and helps in the field, such as digging into caves.

items.title: Redrawn Companion art
items.text: The world, the explorer and the signs are being redrawn at a larger tile size in the game's art style.

items.title: Companion software for the device
items.text: Once the game loop is settled, the Companion's screens move to native code for the real handheld.

modules.name: Caddy
modules.oneLine: The shared dock that charges both handhelds, connects the kit and prints what you find.

items.title: Docking the Companion
items.text: On the sandbox, a stand-in dock beside the Station page moves your crates across when you dock.

items.title: Handing each new mibi to the Caddy
items.text: When a mibi grows, the Station hands it to the Caddy for its finished pictures, and the game plays on with a placeholder if the Caddy cannot be reached.

items.title: The e-paper summary
items.text: A quiet four-grey screen on the Caddy will show your residents, waiting pods and supplies at a glance.

items.title: Printed cards
items.text: The Caddy's printer will feed out a card for a mibi, carrying its genome stamp so it can be scanned back.

items.title: Caddy software for the device
items.text: Once the game loop is settled, the Caddy's screen and printer move to native code for the real dock.

modules.name: Species and genetics
modules.oneLine: Real genetics under every mibi: species built from genomes, and children that inherit from both parents.

items.title: The species workbench
items.text: Build any of the sixteen species from its genome, roll individuals and cross two of them in your browser.

items.title: Inheritance that really works
items.text: Some traits blend between the parents, others show or hide by dominant and recessive copies, and close relatives make weaker crosses.

items.title: The genome stamp
items.text: Every mibi carries a stamp that encodes its real genome, and a phone scan page reads it back.

items.title: Art for all sixteen species
items.text: Each species is getting its finished look; most still show a placeholder for now.

items.title: Mutation
items.text: Rare changes may one day appear during growing, breeding or exploring.

items.title: Growing up and growing old
items.text: Mibis will age from juvenile to adult to elder, with strengths that shift along the way.

items.title: Bonding and care
items.text: Bonding, care and growth will make you attached to particular mibis and curious about their families.

modules.name: Cloud
modules.oneLine: Optional online extras on top of a kit that plays fully on its own.

items.title: A painted look for every mibi
items.text: The full path from growing a mibi to its picture landing runs on the sandbox with stand-in pictures while the painted style is tuned species by species.

items.title: Wireless sync for the Companion
items.text: Your Companion could stay in step with the kit without docking.

items.title: A global mibi exchange
items.text: A place to meet and swap mibis with other players, always with the keeper's consent.

items.title: Lineage records and certificates
items.text: Lasting records of your families, with certificates you can print.

items.title: Mini-games and printer games
items.text: Extra ways to play with your mibis, on screen and on paper.

modules.name: Hardware
modules.oneLine: Open-hardware devices to print and build yourself; nothing physical exists yet, because the game is proven in software first.

items.title: The Station on a Raspberry Pi 4
items.text: The new face is built for the Pi as it is made; running it on a real Pi, with its speed checks, waits until the game plays end to end.

items.title: A bench console
items.text: A Companion reference board with real buttons, running an expedition.

items.title: Screens and controls at real size
items.text: Displays and controls compared side by side against the game's art.

items.title: Power, charging, radio and printing
items.text: Each part tried and measured on the bench before anything is fixed.

items.title: Boards and enclosures
items.text: Boards and 3D-printable cases, designed after the measurements and published as open hardware.

items.title: A small pilot
items.text: A handful of complete kits, assembled with common tools.

modules.name: Website
modules.oneLine: Where to see the kit, play the prototypes and follow the project.

items.title: The homepage
items.text: What Miniature Beasts is, the three devices, and links to play and to the source.

items.title: The sandbox
items.text: Every prototype is published to the sandbox automatically after each change, with the build it is serving in the footer.

items.title: This roadmap
items.text: A public page showing what exists, what is being built and what comes next for each part of the project.

items.title: A real pitch with a playable demo
items.text: A fuller page built around the actual world and creatures, with a playable embedded in it.

items.title: Builder documentation
items.text: Guides for printing, wiring and assembling your own kit.

items.title: Devlog
items.text: Regular notes on what changed and why.

items.title: Kit sign-up
items.text: A way to hear when kits are ready.
